title: Speedometer
prompt: A labelled bench adaptation of the page 46 mechanical car speedometer uses a hand-driven road-speed shaft and flexible rotating-wire cable. Drive rotates the magnet inside the drag cup; magnetic drag deflects the pointer against its hairspring. Accelerate increases shaft speed and pointer deflection. Roll distance continues rotation and advances the distance drums through the worm, eccentric pin, reciprocating drive arm, ratchet and decimal reduction or carry train. See-through exposes those real components. The pointer measures current shaft speed and the drums accumulate distance. Do not drive the pointer rigidly through the odometer gears or add a trip-reset mechanism.
blurb: A bench adaptation separates magnetic speed indication from an eccentric-and-ratchet distance counter.

adaptation.type: Teaching bench, not an exact reconstruction.
adaptation.testInput: A small hand-driven wheel replaces the car transmission.
adaptation.calibration: Illustrative twelve shaft turns per counter metre, not a production calibration.
adaptation.initialReading: Nine metres already travelled. No reset mechanism.
adaptation.geometry: Enlarged schematic teeth, simplified decimal carry tooth profiles and separated supports.
adaptation.motion: All motion follows input shaft turns. Magnet and worm share the input. Pointer follows speed with spring return. Distance advances only on forward ratchet strokes.

editionAccess.2016: saved primary page text and page 46 image inspected

verification.telemetry: n/a. Standalone static figure has no production telemetry.
